task.description: WF-03 Step 4b re-gate 2 (rework 2 of 3) for ISS-0446. Coordinator directed the remedy (narrow the claim, do not build a cross-test guard) rather than leaving TEST-DESIGNER to choose; TEST-DESIGNER independently agreed and additionally argued a cross-test guard would require adding trap_exit/slow-terminate behaviour to the real production Poller. Gate: (1) is the overclaim actually gone, including softened-but-still-false phrasing; (2) is the replacement claim true; (3) is the residual gap stated honestly in both the test and the spec; (4) does REVISION NOTE 2 correct rather than silently soften, leaving REVISION NOTE 1 intact; (5) judge the retained Iss0446RegressionGuard.SlowTrapChild module name; (6) confirm mechanics untouched and file still green. Also gate whether directing the remedy (rather than the fix-site cross-test-guard option) and the rejection of adding trap_exit to the real Poller were the right calls.

result.summary:
VERDICT: PASS. All six gate items hold up under independent verification. No MAJOR or BLOCKER findings. One MINOR recorded per the coordinator's own instruction to record without blocking if worth noting.

=== ITEM 1: IS THE OVERCLAIM ACTUALLY GONE -- YES, verified by direct diff and full read ===
Diffed the exact commit range (git diff 2e248cbb..e00b8fa6 -- test/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher_test.exs) and separately filtered out every comment/blank line to confirm the ONLY non-comment change anywhere in the file is the test's own name string -- zero assertion or call-sequence lines touched. Read the new test name, the full rewritten leading comment, the trailing in-body comment, and the SlowTrapChild moduledoc in full (not skimmed). The old sentence ('so nobody can reintroduce a check-then-act on_exit guard on top of it later') and the old test name's parenthetical '(ISS-0446 regression guard)' are both gone -- not present anywhere, softened or otherwise. Checked specifically for softened-but-still-false phrasing (the coordinator's explicit concern): found none. The new comment states affirmatively and repeatedly what the test does NOT do: 'It does NOT verify, and must not be read as verifying, that nobody can reintroduce a check-then-act on_exit guard at the actual fix site,' names the fix site precisely ('the test directly above this one'), cites the exact validator measurement ('2 of 15 attempts (~13%)'), and states the consequence in the negative, not hedged ('A reintroduction there is NOT reliably caught by this test, or by any other test in this suite'). The trailing in-body comment was also corrected in the same pass ('discriminates a regression in THIS FIXTURE IDIOM ITSELF ... see the scope note above for what that does and does not cover') -- this second, easy-to-miss comment site was not overlooked.

=== ITEM 2: IS THE REPLACEMENT CLAIM TRUE -- YES ===
The test now claims only that 'this suite's own fixture idiom for a throwaway per-test supervisor ... tears down cleanly even under a DELIBERATELY WIDENED shutdown window.' This is exactly what the test's own assertions establish (fetch_test_supervisor/0 + start_supervised!/1, no on_exit, against a trap_exit + Process.sleep(5) child, all four assertions passing) and exactly what re-gate 1's 24 independent clean observations (15 isolated + 8 full-file + 1 full-suite-under-real-contention, 0 failures) already measured. No new overclaim was introduced in the replacement text -- I read the full new comment looking specifically for a fresh overclaim (e.g. an implied 'this is sufficient regression coverage for the fixture idiom class' or similar) and found the language stays scoped to 'this suite's own fixture idiom,' not extended to any other file or a general claim about ExUnit's public contract.

=== ITEM 3: IS THE RESIDUAL GAP STATED HONESTLY, IN BOTH PLACES -- YES ===
Test file: the rewritten leading comment states the gap directly, with the measured figure, in the same paragraph as the retraction (not deferred to a separate location a reader might skip) -- 'A reintroduction there is NOT reliably caught by this test, or by any other test in this suite.' Spec file: read test/specs/ISS-0446.md in full for this gate. REVISION NOTE 2 has a dedicated, explicitly-labeled subsection 'The residual gap, stated plainly, not papered over' that says: 'a reintroduction of the check-then-act pattern AT THE FIX SITE ITSELF ... is not reliably caught by this new test, or by any other test currently in this suite. The only thing standing between a future edit and that regression is REVIEWER's own structural argument at review time ... plus ordinary code review -- not automated test coverage.' This is not softened into reassurance -- it states plainly that automated coverage does not exist for this scenario, names what does substitute for it (structural argument + code review), and explicitly disclaims that this should be read as closed ('it is recorded here so it is not silently assumed closed by the existence of the (differently-scoped) new test'). The 'Coverage check' section's first line was also corrected consistently with this (not just the prose above it) -- confirmed by reading it directly: '(b) does NOT extend to reliably catching a reintroduction at the fix site itself (~13% measured) -- that residual gap rests on (a) plus ordinary code review, not on automated test coverage, and is recorded as open.' Every location I found that touches this claim is internally consistent; no location claims something the others contradict.

=== ITEM 4: DOES REVISION NOTE 2 CORRECT RATHER THAN SILENTLY SOFTEN -- YES ===
Read REVISION NOTE 2 end-to-end. It explicitly retracts ('the committed test's stated PURPOSE was also overclaimed, and has been corrected'), cites both measurements by name and number (validator's 2/15 and TEST-DESIGNER's own independent 0/5 spot-check, both attributed correctly), states the direction taken and the reasoning for rejecting the alternative (the ISS-0378/ISS-0404/ISS-0413 fragility precedent, reasoned through rather than just cited), and closes with the residual-gap paragraph rather than ending on a reassuring note. REVISION NOTE 1 (rework 1's retraction of the original 'async:true only' claim) is untouched -- confirmed by reading lines 22-46 of the current file, byte-for-byte identical in substance to what re-gate 1 already reviewed, still present and not merged into or overwritten by REVISION NOTE 2. Two independent, stacked corrections are visible to a future reader, exactly as they should be.

=== ITEM 5: THE RETAINED MODULE NAME -- ACCEPTABLE, judgment call, not a defect ===
Iss0446RegressionGuard.SlowTrapChild keeps a name that, read in isolation (e.g. in a stack trace or a grep for 'RegressionGuard'), would suggest it guards the ISS-0446 regression. Weighed both ways: a rename would be more literally accurate, but (a) the coordinator's own rework-2 scope was 'name, comment, moduledoc and spec ONLY' with an explicit intent to keep the change narrow and not re-touch mechanics-adjacent surface -- a rename is a larger, more mechanical-feeling change than editing prose, even though it is still just a name; (b) the moduledoc -- the first thing anyone opening this module reads -- states the mismatch explicitly, prominently, and correctly ('per that test's own corrected scope note, it does not guard against a reintroduction of the check-then-act pattern at the ISS-0446 fix site itself -- only against a teardown regression ... in the abstract'), which is exactly the kind of self-correcting traceability comment this project already has precedent for valuing (compare docs/anti-patterns.md style corrections-in-place elsewhere in this same run); (c) grepped for other references to this module name across the tree (`grep -rn Iss0446RegressionGuard test/`) and confirmed it is used only within this one file, so there is no risk of the misleading name propagating into another file's assumptions. On balance this is acceptable as shipped -- a MINOR stylistic quibble at most, not a defect, and not required to change before PASS.

=== ITEM 6: MECHANICS UNTOUCHED, FILE STILL GREEN -- CONFIRMED ===
Per-line diff (git diff 2e248cbb..e00b8fa6, filtered to non-comment/non-blank lines) shows exactly one non-comment change: the test's own name string. No assertion, no call sequence, no fixture behavior, no describe-block structure changed. On that basis I did not re-run the full 24-observation reliability battery from re-gate 1 (isolated x15, full-file x8, full-suite-under-contention x1) -- there is no code-path reason those results could have changed, and re-running a 1445-second full suite for a docstring diff would not be a proportionate use of this gate. I did re-run the actual file once as a live sanity check: `mix test test/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher_test.exs` -> `Finished in 29.9 seconds (0.00s async, 29.9s sync)`, `Result: 43 passed`. Still green, same 43-test count as every prior gate in this run. `git status --porcelain` (repo root) was empty before I ran anything and is empty now -- I made no changes.

=== GATING THE JOINT JUDGMENT CALL (coordinator directing the remedy; rejecting a cross-test guard; rejecting adding trap_exit to the real Poller) ===
Agree with all three calls, independently reasoned, not merely deferred to because two other agents agreed first:
- Directing the remedy rather than leaving it open: reasonable here specifically because my own re-gate 1 handoff already framed this as a binary (narrow vs. build a cross-test guard) with named tradeoffs, so the coordinator was choosing between two options I had already scoped, not overriding an open question I intended to leave to TEST-DESIGNER's judgment. No process concern.
- Rejecting the cross-test guard: correct. A test that reaches into a sibling test's specific construction to detect its mutation is fragile in exactly the shape ISS-0378/ISS-0404/ISS-0413 already established this project deletes tests for (a test coupled to something outside its own declared, stable contract) -- here the coupling would be to a sibling test's internal implementation rather than git history, but the fragility mechanism (an unrelated, legitimate future edit to the fix-site test's own internals breaking the guard for reasons having nothing to do with the race) is the same shape, and TEST-DESIGNER's rework-2 handoff correctly worked through why before agreeing, not just agreeing on say-so.
- Rejecting trap_exit/slow-terminate on the real Poller: correct and not close. Adding test-only timing/exit-trapping behavior to a production module purely to make it instrumentable by a test fixture is a real production-code compromise for testability's sake with no runtime benefit, and would itself need CODE-DESIGNER/REVIEWER/SECURITY-REVIEWER sign-off as a lib/ change to a real supervised worker -- vastly disproportionate to closing a MINOR test-infrastructure gap. Confirmed independently (not just accepted TEST-DESIGNER's framing) by reading Letflow.Engine.ServiceTaskDispatcher.Poller's role: it is a real supervised child in the application tree, not a test-only construct, so this would be a permanent behavioral change to shipped code for a test's convenience.

=== CLEANUP ===
No files created or mutated during this gate beyond reading and running the existing suite once. `git status --porcelain` empty throughout.
